venue: TROPICANA FIELD (1 Tropicana Drive, St. Petersburg, FL 33705). CONFIRMED CURRENT AND IN USE for the 2026 season - this was the flagged high-risk venue check for this project and it resolves cleanly to Tropicana Field. WHY IT WAS AT RISK: Hurricane Milton tore the roof off the building in October 2024 and the Rays did NOT play here in 2025. Ballparks of Baseball, verbatim: 'Hurricane Milton ripped apart the fabric roof leaving the entire interior exposed.' and the club relocated to 'Steinbrenner Field in Tampa, the spring training home of the New York Yankees' for 2025 (https://www.ballparksofbaseball.com/ballparks/tropicana-field/). Wikipedia, verbatim: 'Due to the hurricane damage, the Rays played all of their home games for the 2025 season at George M. Steinbrenner Field in Tampa.' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropicana_Field). THE 2026 RETURN IS CONFIRMED BY FIVE INDEPENDENT DATED SOURCES, three of them published AFTER the 2026 season began: (1) MLB.com club news, dated November 12, 2025, announcing 2026 Tropicana Field upgrades and ticketing, with the CEO quoted that the park would 'look better than it has ever looked' by 'Opening Day on April 6, 2026' (https://www.mlb.com/news/rays-announce-tropicana-field-upgrades-ticket-information-2026). (2) ESPN, November 13, 2025, 'Rays to return to Tropicana Field in '26 after hurricane repairs' (https://www.espn.com/mlb/story/_/id/46947195/rays-return-tropicana-field-26-hurricane-repairs). (3) Rays official press release DATED APRIL 5, 2026, verbatim: 'The Tampa Bay Rays will open the 2026 season at home on Monday, April 6 for a two-team, six-game homestand against the Chicago Cubs' (https://www.mlb.com/press-release/rays-open-the-2026-season-at-tropicana-field-with-a-two-team-six-game-homestand). (4) WUSF, DATED APRIL 6, 2026: 'A full house welcomes baseball back to the Trop. And the Rays respond with a 6-4 win' (https://www.wusf.org/sports/2026-04-06/a-full-house-welcomes-baseball-back-to-the-trop-and-the-rays-respond-with-a-6-4-win) and Bay News 9 same date, 'Welcome home! Rays beat Cubs in emotional Tropicana Field return' (https://baynews9.com/fl/tampa/news/2026/04/06/tampa-bay-rays-chicago-cubs-opening-day-tropicana-field). The 2026 home opener was therefore not merely scheduled but PLAYED at Tropicana Field. (5) Ballparks of Baseball, verbatim: the Rays 'resumed playing at Tropicana Field in 2026' (https://www.ballparksofbaseball.com/ballparks/tropicana-field/). (6) The club's own live 2026 ballpark pages are served under the Tropicana Field name (https://www.mlb.com/rays/ballpark/information/guide, https://www.mlb.com/rays/ballpark/information/accessibility-guide, https://www.mlb.com/rays/ballpark/netting), and the MLB.com ballpark guide page carries a date of April 9, 2026 (https://www.mlb.com/news/featured/tropicana-field-guide-capacity-seating-chart-parking-and-more). RateYourSeats serves the venue at slug 'tropicana-field' with per-section pages carrying 'Verified Feb 2026' stamps (e.g. https://www.rateyourseats.com/tropicana-field/seating/sections/148, https://www.rateyourseats.com/tropicana-field/seating/sections/150, https://www.rateyourseats.com/tropicana-field/seating/sections/141) and '(2026 Review)' expert-review stamps (e.g. https://www.rateyourseats.com/tropicana-field/seating/sections/102, https://www.rateyourseats.com/tropicana-field/seating/sections/120, https://www.rateyourseats.com/tropicana-field/seating/sections/203), and its Baldwin Club zone page is stamped 'Last verified and reviewed: March 2026' (https://www.rateyourseats.com/tropicana-field/seating/rays-club). STALE SOURCES TO IGNORE: any source stating the Rays play at George M. Steinbrenner Field - that was TRUE FOR THE 2025 SEASON ONLY and is now stale. Examples of now-stale pages that still rank in search: https://www.mlb.com/press-release/press-release-tampa-bay-rays-to-play-2025-season-at-george-m-steinbrenner-field-in-tampa and https://www.mlb.com/rays/news/rays-home-playoff-games-george-m-steinbrenner-field. There is NO temporary or reduced-size venue in play for 2026, so the ticketing source serves normal per-section pages, not generic zone pages - the contingency raised in the assignment did not materialise. NAMING RIGHTS - NO STADIUM RENAME. Wikipedia, verbatim: 'Tropicana Products signed a 30-year naming rights deal in October 1996' and although PepsiCo bought Tropicana in 1998, 'the company refrained from making any changes to the park's naming rights' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropicana_Field). The building is still Tropicana Field in 2026. CRITICAL DISTINCTION - AREA NAMING RIGHTS ARE NOT STADIUM NAMING RIGHTS. Several INTERIOR spaces carry 2026 corporate sponsor names that must NOT be mistaken for a stadium rename: 'DEX Home Plate Club' / 'DEX Imaging Home Plate Club', 'The Baldwin Group Club', 'Republic Bank Draft Room' (also written 'Republic Draft Room'), 'Webull Suite Level', 'MaintenX SkyDeck', 'Budweiser Porch', 'Viva Victory Ledge', 'Dream Finders Homes Terrace', 'RIPA Bullpen Box', 'Seminole Hard Rock Tampa 162 Landing', 'Daiquiri Deck', 'Cownose Clubhouse', 'Orlando Health St. Petersburg' (first aid) - all sourced from https://www.mlb.com/rays/ballpark/information/guide and https://www.mlb.com/rays/ballpark/information/accessibility-guide. This is the same trap as UNIQLO at Dodger Stadium: sponsor names attached to spaces inside the park, not to the park.

capacity: 25,025 for the standard baseball configuration WITH THE UPPER DECK CLOSED. This is the figure carried by every source checked, but NOTE: no 2026-dated statement of capacity from the Rays themselves was found - the club's own 2026 ballpark guide (https://www.mlb.com/rays/ballpark/information/guide) does not state a capacity at all. (1) MLB.com ballpark guide, page dated April 9, 2026, verbatim: '25,025 (since 2019, with upper deck closed)' (https://www.mlb.com/news/featured/tropicana-field-guide-capacity-seating-chart-parking-and-more). (2) Ballparks of Baseball, verbatim: current capacity '25,025 (2019)' with previous levels '31,042 (2014-2018), 42,735' (https://www.ballparksofbaseball.com/ballparks/tropicana-field/). (3) Wikipedia: 'The stadium's capacity stands at 25,025 (2019-present), with upper decks tarped over.' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropicana_Field). (4) ArenaCapacity, page 'Updated Apr 2, 2026', verbatim: 'Tropicana Field can accommodate up to 25,000 fans, creating a cozy atmosphere for Rays games.' and 'Prior to 2019, the upper deck was closed to further reduce the standard seating capacity to 25,025, though tarps covering over 10,000 seats can be removed for high-demand events such as playoffs, increasing capacity to over 42,000.' (https://www.arenacapacity.com/tropicana-field-seating-capacity/). (5) Historic, Andrew Clem vital statistics: 'The original capacity was 45,200, but was reduced several times after 2002'; 2018 capacity 'rose from 31,042 to 42,735'; 2019 'reduced...from 42,735 to 25,025' (http://www.andrewclem.com/Baseball/TropicanaField.html). SO: ~25,025 for regular-season games, ~42,000+ if the 300-level tarps come off for the postseason. See `levels` for the 300-level closure, which is the single most consequential capacity fact at this park.

orientation.summary: WEAK - ONE SOURCE ONLY, and it is a domed stadium so the usual sun/shade corroboration is unavailable. Andrew Clem's vital-statistics table lists the orientation as 'NE' (http://www.andrewclem.com/Baseball/TropicanaField.html). Read in Clem's usual convention that is the bearing from home plate out toward centre field, i.e. THE BATTER FACES ROUGHLY NORTH-EAST. Treat as low-to-medium confidence: it is a single non-official source and no bearing is stated anywhere on the club's own pages, on Wikipedia, or on Ballparks of Baseball.
orientation.batter_faces: NORTH-EAST (single source, low-to-medium confidence - see summary)
orientation.sun_and_shade: NOT APPLICABLE. Tropicana Field is a FIXED-ROOF DOME - Wikipedia: 'Non-retractable fiberglass dome' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropicana_Field). There is no sun exposure anywhere in the seating bowl, so no shade/sun guidance should be generated for any section at this park. This is a genuine difference from every open-air park in the project.
orientation.roof: Verbatim, Andrew Clem: 'The apex of the roof is 225 feet above the field, directly above a point just in front of second base' (http://www.andrewclem.com/Baseball/TropicanaField.html). The roof is deliberately TILTED - The Stadium Reviews, verbatim: 'The Domed Stadium for the Tampa Bay Rays had a slanted roof for two primary reasons' (hurricane wind loads and cooling costs), and 'With the roof tilting in the outfield, you have the catwalks at a lower height' (https://thestadiumreviews.com/blogs/info/why-is-tropicana-field-tilted/). The roof was destroyed by Hurricane Milton in Oct 2024 and rebuilt; the city and team spent 'nearly $60 million in repairs' before the 2026 return (https://www.ballparksofbaseball.com/ballparks/tropicana-field/).
orientation.dimensions: Verbatim, Ballparks of Baseball: '315-L, 404-C, 322-R.' (https://www.ballparksofbaseball.com/ballparks/tropicana-field/). Wikipedia agrees: 'Left Field: 315 ft; Right Field: 322 ft; Center Field: 404 ft' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropicana_Field). Backstop distance 'only 50 feet' (http://www.andrewclem.com/Baseball/TropicanaField.html).

numbering_direction.scheme: PARITY - NOT A SWEEP. *** THIS PARK DOES NOT NUMBER ONE WAY ROUND THE BOWL. *** Tropicana Field numbers OUTWARD FROM HOME PLATE BY PARITY: ODD sections run from home plate down the THIRD-BASE line and on into LEFT field; EVEN sections run from home plate down the FIRST-BASE line and on into RIGHT field. Both parities start low at home plate and increase with distance from home plate. This is exactly the parity signature the discovery brief warns about, and it CHANGES THE GENERATOR'S CONFIG SCHEMA, not just its values: there is no single 'increases toward first base' or 'increases toward third base' answer for this park, and any config that assumes a single sweep direction WILL BE WRONG FOR HALF THE BALLPARK. The same parity rule holds on EVERY tier checked (100 level, 200/Press level, 300 level, and the SkyDeck).
numbering_direction.answer_to_the_sweep_question: NEITHER. The park does not sweep one way round the bowl at all. Section numbers increase outward from home plate in BOTH directions simultaneously, split by odd/even parity.
parity_signature_verbatim: THE CLUB'S OWN GUIDE (highest authority, 2026-live): 'Even-numbered sections are on the first base/right field side...Odd-numbered sections are on the third base/left field side.' (https://www.mlb.com/rays/ballpark/information/guide)

THE CLUB'S OWN NETTING STATEMENT - this is the textbook parity signature described in the brief, an odd number and an even number naming the two SYMMETRIC foul poles: 'Protective netting extends from home plate to the foul poles located in Sections 137 and 138.' (https://www.mlb.com/rays/ballpark/information/guide and https://www.mlb.com/rays/ballpark/netting). 137 is the LEFT-field foul pole (odd/third base) and 138 is the RIGHT-field foul pole (even/first base). Under any single-sweep numbering these two consecutive numbers could not sit at OPPOSITE foul poles.

Verbatim: 'Sections 101-108: Rows L-N, positioned behind the Home Plate Club seats' (https://www.rateyourseats.com/tropicana-field/seating/sections/101, https://www.rateyourseats.com/tropicana-field/seating/sections/102). Corroborated by the club: the Gate 4 elevator serves 'DEX Home Plate Club, Section 101' (https://www.mlb.com/rays/ballpark/information/accessibility-guide), and First Aid is 'between Gates 3 and 4 on the 100 Level, behind home plate' (https://www.mlb.com/rays/ballpark/information/guide).
three_required_anchors.LEFT FIELD (odd, high): Sections 141, 143, 145, 147, 149. Verbatim: 'Sections 141-145 see a fair share of home run balls in the first ten rows' contrasted with Right Field even sections (https://www.rateyourseats.com/tropicana-field/seating/sections/141, https://www.rateyourseats.com/tropicana-field/seating/sections/149); both are zoned 'Lower Level Outfield (Baseball)'. INDEPENDENT CORROBORATION: the MaintenX SkyDeck is 'located above left field' per the club (https://www.mlb.com/rays/ballpark/information/guide) and its sections are 341, 343, 345, 347, 349, 351, 353, 355 - ALL ODD, WITHOUT EXCEPTION. RateYourSeats: 'Sections 341-355 in left field' (https://www.rateyourseats.com/tropicana-field/seating/sections/345). An all-odd tier sitting over left field is decisive independent proof that odd = left/third-base side.

hard_fact_cross_checks: BULLPENS (RateYourSeats, section 129): 'The Rays bullpen can be found in front of sections 128 and 130, while the visiting team bullpen is on the opposite side of the field at 127 and 129.' (https://www.rateyourseats.com/tropicana-field/seating/sections/129). Rays bullpen = EVEN sections = first-base side; visitors = ODD = third-base side. This matches the club's own dugout statement exactly (Rays on first base), so parity is confirmed by two independent facts pointing the same way.

DUGOUT (club, verbatim): 'The Rays dugout is on the first base side, and the visitor's dugout is on the third base side.' (https://www.mlb.com/rays/ballpark/information/guide) + RateYourSeats places section 118 (EVEN) 'above the Rays dugout' (https://www.rateyourseats.com/tropicana-field/seating/sections/118). Even = first base. Consistent.

ELEVATORS (club, verbatim, https://www.mlb.com/rays/ballpark/information/accessibility-guide): 'Gate 2 elevator stops: Gate 2, Section 132' vs 'Gate 6 elevator stops: Gate 6, Section 131, Webull Suite Level, MaintenX SkyDeck'. Consecutive numbers 131 and 132 are served by DIFFERENT gates on OPPOSITE sides of the park, and the gate serving ODD 131 is the same gate that serves the SkyDeck 'above left field'. Under a single sweep, 131 and 132 would be neighbours sharing a gate. Further: 'Gate 1 elevator stops: Gate 1, Cownose Clubhouse, Section 150' - 150 (even) is in right field, reached from a different gate again. Gate and elevator statements are the hardest facts available and they all corroborate parity.

NETTING RUN (club, https://www.mlb.com/rays/ballpark/netting): the netted list is a CONTIGUOUS integer run '101, 102, 103, ... 137, and 138' terminating at the two foul poles. Under parity this is exactly right - it covers both foul lines out to both poles. Under a single sweep it would be geometrically impossible for a contiguous run to end at both poles at once.
numbering_direction.increases_toward: OUTWARD FROM HOME PLATE, BOTH WAYS. Odd -> toward third base then left field. Even -> toward first base then right field. There is no single 'toward first base' / 'toward third base' answer; do not force one.
numbering_direction.confidence: VERY HIGH. The parity rule is stated in plain words by the club itself, restated independently by RateYourSeats on four different section pages spanning two tiers, and corroborated by four hard structural facts (netting termini, dugouts, bullpens, elevator/gate assignments) plus an all-odd left-field tier. Nothing found contradicts it.

levels.name: 100 Level (club's name: '100 Level (Field Level)'; RateYourSeats: 'Lower Level')
levels.notes: Full 50-section lower bowl, 101-150, split by parity: odd 101-149 third base then left field, even 102-150 first base then right field. RateYourSeats sub-zones, verbatim: 'Lower Level Infield seating at Tropicana Field includes sections 101-126'; 'Lower Level Down the Line (Baseball)' for the 127-136 range (seen on 129, 130, 136); 'Lower Level Outfield (Baseball)' for the outfield sections (seen on 141, 144, 148, 149, 150). Foul poles are AT sections 137 (left) and 138 (right), so 139-150 are true outfield seating. Premium sub-areas embedded in this level include the 'Fieldside Boxes' (e.g. 118, 120) and a 'Chalk Box' - 'Located at the very front of Sections 122, 124, and 126 along the first base line' in rows A-D (https://www.rateyourseats.com/tropicana-field/seating/sections/126).

levels.name: 200 Level (club's name: '200 Level'; RateYourSeats: 'Press Level')
levels.notes: 22 sections, 203-224. Starts at 203 - there is no 200, 201 or 202 in the index. Parity holds: 'odd sections on the third base side' (203) and 'Even-numbered sections: First base side (Rays side)' (224). A PRESS BOX sits directly behind home plate and splits the tier: 'separated by a press box directly behind home plate, with even numbered sections 204-210 closer to 1st base' (204). Verbatim descriptions: 'Middle level seating is located in the 200 level of Tropicana field along the 1st base line' (224); 'Sections 203-224 provide a higher vantage point for seeing the full field' (203, 224). All rows on this tier are short: A-H. NAME CONFLICT: RateYourSeats calls this tier 'Press Level'; the club's own guide calls it '200 Level' and separately lists a 'Club Level' and a 'Webull Suite Level (200 Level Premium Suites)'. Recorded in `uncertain`.

levels.name: 300 Level / Upper Deck
levels.notes: *** CLOSED / TARPED FOR REGULAR-SEASON PLAY - THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT CAVEAT AT THIS PARK. *** RateYourSeats still serves live per-section pages for 300-324 (300, 301, 312 and 324 individually confirmed), so the sections EXIST in the ticketing source's index, but they have not been sold for regular-season games since 2019. Wikipedia: capacity '25,025 (2019-present), with upper decks tarped over' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropicana_Field). MLB.com ballpark guide (April 9, 2026): '25,025 (since 2019, with upper deck closed)'. WTSP, verbatim: 'The reconfiguration of the ballpark will eliminate the upper-deck 300 level', decreasing capacity 'to an estimated 25,000-26,000 fans' (https://www.wtsp.com/article/sports/mlb/rays/rays-are-getting-rid-of-upper-level-seats-at-tropicana-field-to-create-intimate-fan-experience/67-bce96bde-f13e-4f79-86aa-df67ddbc51ec). ArenaCapacity (Updated Apr 2, 2026): 'tarps covering over 10,000 seats can be removed for high-demand events such as playoffs, increasing capacity to over 42,000'. There is precedent for partial re-opening: 'Rays to open portions of upper deck for Yankees series' (https://www.mlb.com/news/rays-to-open-portions-of-upper-deck-for-yankees-series). NO 2026-DATED OFFICIAL STATEMENT was found either confirming or lifting the closure for the 2026 season, and the club's 2026 guide still lists a '300 Level' among its levels while its elevator list names NO 300-level stop. TREAT AS CLOSED FOR REGULAR SEASON, AVAILABLE FOR POSTSEASON, and flag to the user. Parity is assumed to hold here on the strength of the club's park-wide rule, but RateYourSeats prints no explicit odd/even sentence on any 300-level page checked - see `uncertain`.

levels.name: MaintenX SkyDeck (upper level, above left field)
levels.notes: ALL-ODD deck, 341/343/345/347/349/351/353/355, sitting over LEFT field - a decisive independent corroboration of the odd=left-field parity rule. Club, verbatim: 'The MaintenX SkyDeck introduces a vibrant new all-inclusive experience located above left field.' (https://www.mlb.com/rays/ballpark/information/guide). RateYourSeats: 'Sections 341-355 in left field', with 341-345 'down the left field line in foul territory' (https://www.rateyourseats.com/tropicana-field/seating/sections/345). Rows are A-F plus a WCH row, 'with wheelchair seating behind Row F'. Served by the Gate 6 elevator and has its own Guest Services desk (https://www.mlb.com/rays/ballpark/information/accessibility-guide). Never wraps behind home plate.

levels.name: Club / premium field level - DEX Imaging Home Plate Club and The Baldwin Group Club
levels.notes: TWO distinct premium products that RateYourSeats serves as per-section pages under letter-suffixed URL slugs. (a) HOME PLATE CLUB - slugs HPC103, HPC104, HPC107, HPC108; page heading is written 'Home Plate Club 103 at Tropicana Field'; 'located in four exclusive sections directly behind home plate, positioned at field level'; rows D-J (https://www.rateyourseats.com/tropicana-field/seating/sections/HPC103). The club now brands it 'DEX Home Plate Club' / 'DEX Imaging Home Plate Club'. (b) RAYS CLUB / BALDWIN GROUP CLUB - slugs 106C, 108C, 110C, 112C, 114C, 116C, 118C, 120C, 122C, 124C, 126C (all EVEN base numbers = first-base side); page heading is written 'Rays Club 106 at Tropicana Field'; rows PP-UU (https://www.rateyourseats.com/tropicana-field/seating/sections/106C). Zone page: 'Sections 106-126 along the first base line', 'Last verified and reviewed: March 2026' (https://www.rateyourseats.com/tropicana-field/seating/rays-club), where the zone is titled 'Baldwin Club' / 'Baldwin Group Club'. The club's own 2026 guide names it 'The Baldwin Group Club' and places it 'on the fourth floor' (https://www.mlb.com/rays/news/rays-continue-tropicana-field-improvements-ahead-of-opening-day, Feb 27 2026) - NOTE that conflicts with the RateYourSeats 'along the first base line' field-level placement; see `uncertain`. IDENTIFIER WARNING: the URL slug (106C) and the displayed heading ('Rays Club 106') differ; `sections` records the SLUG form because that is the addressable per-section identifier.

dugouts.source_verbatim: The club's own ballpark guide, verbatim: 'The Rays dugout is on the first base side, and the visitor's dugout is on the third base side.' (https://www.mlb.com/rays/ballpark/information/guide).
dugouts.corroboration: Ballparks of Baseball, verbatim: 'The home dugout is positioned at first base.' (https://www.ballparksofbaseball.com/ballparks/tropicana-field/). RateYourSeats places section 118 (EVEN) 'above the Rays dugout' (https://www.rateyourseats.com/tropicana-field/seating/sections/118) and describes sections 119-125 as those that 'Extend further down the baselines past the dugouts' (https://www.rateyourseats.com/tropicana-field/seating/sections/120, https://www.rateyourseats.com/tropicana-field/seating/sections/125); section 120 notes 'Sections directly above both Rays and visiting team dugouts'. RateYourSeats also labels the even side 'First base side (Rays side)' (https://www.rateyourseats.com/tropicana-field/seating/sections/224). THREE INDEPENDENT SOURCES AGREE - no conflict, unlike the Progressive Field case cited in the brief.

bullpens: BOTH BULLPENS ARE IN FOUL TERRITORY DOWN THE LINES, IN FRONT OF THE LOWER-BOWL SEATS, one per side. RateYourSeats, verbatim: 'The Rays bullpen can be found in front of sections 128 and 130, while the visiting team bullpen is on the opposite side of the field at 127 and 129.' (https://www.rateyourseats.com/tropicana-field/seating/sections/129, and the same statement appears on https://www.rateyourseats.com/tropicana-field/seating/sections/130). So: RAYS (home) bullpen = in front of EVEN sections 128 and 130 = FIRST-BASE / right-field side, matching the Rays dugout. VISITORS' bullpen = in front of ODD sections 127 and 129 = THIRD-BASE / left-field side, matching the visitors' dugout. Wikipedia agrees on the general placement: 'Bullpens located along left and right field foul lines' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropicana_Field). Andrew Clem notes fans can dine at tabletops in 'special areas next to the bullpens' along the foul lines (http://www.andrewclem.com/Baseball/TropicanaField.html); the club sells a 'RIPA Bullpen Box' product (https://www.mlb.com/rays/ballpark/information/guide) and A View From My Seat lists a 'Bullpen Box' area (https://aviewfrommyseat.com/venue/Tropicana+Field/). NOTE the useful consequence for seat guidance: fans in 127-130 have a bullpen between them and the field.
special_areas: Named areas at Tropicana Field for 2026, from the club's own guide and accessibility guide unless noted. PREMIUM CLUBS AND SUITES: 'DEX Home Plate Club' / 'DEX Imaging Home Plate Club' (behind the backstop, field level, sections HPC103/104/107/108); 'The Baldwin Group Club' (RateYourSeats 'Rays Club' / 'Baldwin Club', sections 106C-126C even, first base line); 'The Tropicana Room' - 'Inside The Baldwin Group Club; now serves as exclusive dining area and lounge for DEX Imaging Home Plate Club members'; 'Republic Bank Draft Room' (also written 'Republic Draft Room'); 'Webull Suite Level' = '200 Level Premium Suites'; 'Executive Suites' - 'Behind home plate on the main concourse level'; Infield Suites AAA-GGG - 'a collection of seven sections directly behind home plate, positioned just above the main seating bowl'. DECKS, LEDGES AND SOCIAL SPACES: 'MaintenX SkyDeck' - 'a vibrant new all-inclusive experience located above left field' (sections 341-355 odd); 'Left Field Ledge' (RateYourSeats zone page, group/party area with table-style seating); 'Viva Victory Ledge' - 'overlooking Left Field'; 'Budweiser Porch' (A View From My Seat also lists a 'Budweiser Patio'); 'Daiquiri Deck'; 'Dream Finders Homes Terrace'; 'RIPA Bullpen Box'; 'Seminole Hard Rock Tampa 162 Landing'; 'Cownose Clubhouse' / 'Cownose Clubhouse Experience' (served by the Gate 1 elevator); 'Field Party Deck' (RateYourSeats zone, URL slug 'mlpd'); 'Center Field Deck' and 'Center Field Porch' (A View From My Seat). IN-PARK ATTRACTIONS: the RAY TANK / touch tank - Ballparks of Baseball, verbatim: 'Rays Touch Tank, a 35-foot, 10,000-gallon tank, where fans can touch live rays' located 'just beyond the fence in right-center field' (https://www.ballparksofbaseball.com/ballparks/tropicana-field/). It directly affects seat guidance in section 150 - RateYourSeats Q&A, verbatim: 'For fans sitting in section 150, seat 9 is directly next to the ray tank in rows W-Z and AA-BB, while seat 12 is next to the tank in all other rows.' (https://www.rateyourseats.com/tropicana-field/seating/sections/150, 'Verified Feb 2026'). Also 'The Beach' - Ballparks of Baseball describes a designated area in LEFT field with 'beach decor and tropical foliage' (https://www.ballparksofbaseball.com/ballparks/tropicana-field/); no 2026-dated club source was found confirming The Beach still exists, so treat as possibly historic. COMMEMORATIVE SEATS (MLB.com ballpark guide, April 9 2026): 'The golden seat in Section 148 is where the Devil Rays' first home run was hit'; 'the golden seat in Section 144 marks where Boggs' 3,000th hit landed'; 'The white seat is where Dan Johnson hit his two-out, game-tying homer'; 'The memorialized seat is just above the right-field walkway' (https://www.mlb.com/news/featured/tropicana-field-guide-capacity-seating-chart-parking-and-more). Note 144 and 148 are EVEN = right field, consistent with the parity rule. 2026 UPGRADES (MLB.com, Nov 12 2025): 'expanded main videoboard, new video displays behind home plate and along both foul poles, a new sound system and refreshed suite interiors' (https://www.mlb.com/news/rays-announce-tropicana-field-upgrades-ticket-information-2026).
accessibility: All quotes from the club's own Tropicana Field Accessibility Guide (https://www.mlb.com/rays/ballpark/information/accessibility-guide) and ballpark guide (https://www.mlb.com/rays/ballpark/information/guide), both live in 2026. SEATING: 'Accessible and companion seating is available throughout Tropicana Field at a variety of price levels.' NOTE: THE CLUB PUBLISHES NO LIST OF ACCESSIBLE SECTION NUMBERS - do not invent one. The only per-section evidence found is the row label 'WCH' appearing in RateYourSeats row lists, e.g. section 120 'Rows in Section 120 are labeled B-Z, AA-JJ, WCH' (https://www.rateyourseats.com/tropicana-field/seating/sections/120) and SkyDeck section 345 'Rows A-F, WCH' described as 'wheelchair seating behind Row F' (https://www.rateyourseats.com/tropicana-field/seating/sections/345). See `row_seat_conventions` for the WCH convention. A View From My Seat carries fan-tagged wheelchair seats at this venue as a fallback data source (https://aviewfrommyseat.com/venue/Tropicana+Field/tag/2/this+seat+is+a+wheelchair+accessible+seat/). GATES: 'All gates are wheelchair accessible.' Gates 1-6 provide access; 'VIP Gate 4 is open to suite holders, DEX Home Plate Club ticket holders, The Baldwin Group Club ticket holders.' 'Gates open 90 minutes before first pitch for Monday-Friday Rays home games and two hours before first pitch on Opening Day and Saturday-Sunday Rays home games.' ELEVATORS - 'Located at Gates 1, 2, 4, and 6', with these stops, verbatim: 'Gate 1 elevator stops: Gate 1, Cownose Clubhouse, Section 150'; 'Gate 2 elevator stops: Gate 2, Section 132'; 'Gate 4 elevator stops: DEX Home Plate Club, Section 101, Republic Draft Room & The Baldwin Group Club, Webull Suite Level'; 'Gate 6 elevator stops: Gate 6, Section 131, Webull Suite Level, MaintenX SkyDeck'. NOTE: NO ELEVATOR STOP IS LISTED FOR ANY 300-LEVEL SECTION, consistent with the upper deck being closed. WHEELCHAIR TRANSPORT: 'wheelchair transport service. The Rolling Rays are available at Gates 1 and 5 on a first-come, first-served basis.' PARKING: 'Lots 1 and 7 offer wheelchair-accessible parking just outside the gates, with the majority of the spaces located in Lot 7' and 'ADA Accessible Parking - Located in Lots 1 and 7 (subject to availability).' SERVICE ANIMALS: 'Service animals trained to perform specific tasks for individuals with disabilities are welcome at Tropicana Field.' SENSORY: sensory bags available at Guest Services containing noise-cancelling headphones and fidget items; 'Sensory Room was designed to provide a safe space for anyone with sensory processing needs.' GUEST SERVICES: located at Gates 1, 3, 4, and the MaintenX SkyDeck. FIRST AID: 'First Aid presented by Orlando Health St. Petersburg can be found between Gates 3 and 4 on the 100 Level, behind home plate.' CLIMATE: the fixed dome makes this a fully indoor, climate-controlled venue - materially relevant to heat-sensitive and mobility-impaired guests in a Florida summer, and it removes sun exposure as a seat-selection factor entirely.
row_seat_conventions: ROWS ARE LETTERED THROUGHOUT, NOT NUMBERED - at every tier checked. The lower bowl uses a single-letter run then DOUBLE letters (A-Z, then AA, BB, CC...), and several lower-bowl sections have a further discontinuous double-letter block. Observed row labels, verbatim from RateYourSeats: 100 LEVEL INFIELD - 101: 'Rows in Section 101 are labeled L-Z, AA-JJ'; 102: 'L-Z, AA-JJ'; 110: 'B-Z, AA-JJ'; 118: 'K-Z, AA-JJ'; 120: 'B-Z, AA-JJ, WCH'; 125: 'B-Z, AA-JJ, PP-XX'; 126: 'A-Z, AA-JJ'. 100 LEVEL DOWN THE LINE - 129: 'G-Z, AA-JJ, PP-XX'; 130: 'G-Z, AA-JJ, PP-XX'; 136: 'G-Z, AA-JJ'. 100 LEVEL OUTFIELD - 141: 'T-Z, AA-WW'; 144: 'T-Z, AA-YY'; 148: 'T-Z, AA-VV'; 149: 'T-Z, AA-RR'; 150: 'T-Z, AA-RR'. NOTE the outfield sections START AT ROW T, not row A - the front rows do not exist there. Lettering start points vary widely by section (A, B, G, K, L or T), so DO NOT assume a uniform first row. 200 / PRESS LEVEL - short tier, rows A-H throughout (203, 204, 224). 300 / UPPER DECK - 300: 'For most events, rows in Section 300 are labeled A-Z, AA-DD'; 301: 'A-Z, AA-DD'; 312: 'A-Z, AA-NN'; 324: 'Rows A-O'. MAINTENX SKYDECK - 345: 'Rows A-F, WCH'. PREMIUM - Home Plate Club 103: 'Rows in Home Plate Club 103 are labeled D-J'; Rays Club 106: 'Rows in Rays Club 106 are labeled PP-UU'. The 'Chalk Box' occupies 'rows A-D' at 'the very front of Sections 122, 124, and 126' (https://www.rateyourseats.com/tropicana-field/seating/sections/126). *** ACCESSIBLE ROW CONVENTION: 'WCH' *** Wheelchair/accessible positions are labelled as a row called WCH, appended AFTER the last lettered row of the section - e.g. section 120 'B-Z, AA-JJ, WCH' and SkyDeck 345 'A-F, WCH' explicitly described as 'wheelchair seating behind Row F'. So WCH is a REAR row, at the back of the section by the concourse, not a front row. Treat 'WCH' as a row label, not a section suffix. SEATS PER ROW vary a lot; small sections exist - section 126, verbatim: 'Section 126, down the right field line at the Trop, features just 10 seats in each row' and it is 'one of the smallest sections in the lower level' (https://www.rateyourseats.com/tropicana-field/seating/sections/126, 'Verified Feb 2026'). Outfield rows are wide: 24 seats in the full rows of 141 and 148, but 'Rows W-Z and AA-BB have 18 seats each' in 148, and section 150 has rows of 9 (in W-Z, AA-BB) or 12 seats. ENTRANCES are sometimes noted by row, e.g. section 126: 'an entrance to this section is located at Row JJ' (https://www.rateyourseats.com/tropicana-field/seating/sections/126).
seat1_side_verbatim: *** SEAT 1 IS ON THE FAN'S LEFT, PARK-WIDE, AND THIS IS CONFIRMED ON BOTH HALVES OF THE BALLPARK. *** THE BOILERPLATE. RateYourSeats prints, IDENTICALLY on every Tropicana Field section page checked: "When looking towards the field/field, lower number seats are on the left". (Note the doubled word 'field/field' - that is exactly how it renders on this venue's pages; at other parks in this project it renders 'field/field/stage'.) Verified verbatim on 25 pages spanning every tier and both halves of the park: 101, 102, 110, 118, 120, 125, 126, 129, 130, 136, 141, 144, 148, 149, 150 (100 level); 203, 204, 224 (Press level); 300, 301, 312, 324 (upper deck); 345 (SkyDeck); HPC103 (Home Plate Club); 106C (Rays Club). WHY THE USUAL WARNING APPLIES WITH FORCE HERE, AND WHY IT NEVERTHELESS PASSES. The brief warns that this park-wide boilerplate was correct on one half and wrong on the other at two parks so far. Tropicana Field is precisely the kind of park where that failure mode is expected, because its sections are MIRRORED about home plate by parity - a park that mirrors its SECTION numbering could easily mirror its SEAT numbering too, putting seat 1 on the inside (home-plate side) of every section and therefore on the LEFT on one half and on the RIGHT on the other. IT DOES NOT. Per-section question-and-answer text, which per the brief BEATS the boilerplate, was found on BOTH halves and BOTH agree with the boilerplate: (a) ODD / THIRD-BASE / LEFT-FIELD HALF - section 141, verbatim: 'There are a total 24 seats in Section 141 Row T. As you face the field, Seat 1 will be on the aisle at the left side of the row, and Seat 24 will be on the aisle at the right.' (https://www.rateyourseats.com/tropicana-field/seating/sections/141, 'Verified Feb 2026'). (b) EVEN / FIRST-BASE / RIGHT-FIELD HALF - section 148, verbatim Q: 'How many seats are in row T section 148 at the Trop?' A: 'There are 24 seats in this row with seat 1 on your left as you look towards the field. Rows W-Z and AA-BB have 18 seats each, while all other rows have 24 seats like in row T.' (https://www.rateyourseats.com/tropicana-field/seating/sections/148, 'Verified Feb 2026'). NO DISAGREEMENT WAS FOUND ANYWHERE between the boilerplate and per-section text. CONCLUSION FOR THE GENERATOR: seat numbering runs uniformly LEFT-to-RIGHT as the fan faces the field, in every section, on both sides of the park. SEAT NUMBERING DOES NOT MIRROR EVEN THOUGH SECTION NUMBERING DOES - this asymmetry is the single most counter-intuitive fact about Tropicana Field and must not be 'corrected' by a later step. A THIRD, INDIRECT CORROBORATION on the even side, recorded as supporting evidence rather than a direct statement: section 150 Q&A, verbatim, 'For fans sitting in section 150, seat 9 is directly next to the ray tank in rows W-Z and AA-BB, while seat 12 is next to the tank in all other rows.' (https://www.rateyourseats.com/tropicana-field/seating/sections/150). Since 150 is the outermost even section and the ray tank sits beyond it in right-CENTRE field (https://www.ballparksofbaseball.com/ballparks/tropicana-field/), the seat adjacent to the tank is the one furthest from home plate in the row, and it is the HIGHEST-numbered seat (9 or 12, the row lengths) - i.e. low numbers sit away from centre field, consistent with seat 1 on the fan's left. FLAGGED AS INFERENCE, not a quoted statement.
known_obstructions: (1) 200-LEVEL OVERHANG over the back of the lower bowl. RateYourSeats, verbatim: 'Avoid Rows WW and XX on the Lower Level because of the obstructed view created by the 200 level overhang.' (https://www.rateyourseats.com/tropicana-field/seating/sections/118). This bites specifically in the lower-bowl sections whose row lists include the PP-XX block - observed at sections 125, 129 and 130 ('G-Z, AA-JJ, PP-XX' / 'B-Z, AA-JJ, PP-XX'). Sections that stop at JJ (e.g. 101, 102, 110, 118, 126, 136) have no WW/XX rows and are unaffected. (2) THE CATWALKS - AN IN-PLAY RULE, NOT A VIEW OBSTRUCTION. Four ring-shaped catwalks hang over fair territory. Wikipedia: 'Four catwalks (A, B, C, D rings) support the dome structure' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropicana_Field). The Stadium Reviews: 'There are four catwalks (A, B, C, and D) that hang over the playing field at The Trop.' and 'When a ball hits the C or D ring, you automatically have the ruling as a home run.' (https://thestadiumreviews.com/blogs/info/why-is-tropicana-field-tilted/). Andrew Clem: 'the two inner catwalks are in play, while any ball hitting the two outer catwalks in fair territory are home runs' (http://www.andrewclem.com/Baseball/TropicanaField.html). These affect PLAY, not sightlines; do not report them as obstructed-view warnings. They do occasionally make a batted ball hard to TRACK for fans. (3) NETTING - see below; netting is in front of sections 101-138 and its 'height and coverage of the netting varies by section' (https://www.mlb.com/rays/ballpark/netting). (4) BULLPENS in front of sections 127, 128, 129 and 130 sit between those seats and the field (https://www.rateyourseats.com/tropicana-field/seating/sections/129). (5) NARROW SECTION - 126 has 'just 10 seats in each row' (https://www.rateyourseats.com/tropicana-field/seating/sections/126); not an obstruction but a capacity/geometry quirk worth surfacing. NETTING EXTENT, VERBATIM FROM THE CLUB (https://www.mlb.com/rays/ballpark/information/guide and https://www.mlb.com/rays/ballpark/netting): 'Protective netting extends from home plate to the foul poles located in Sections 137 and 138.' Full netted list, verbatim: 'Netting Sections: 101, 102, 103, 104, 105, 106, 107, 108, 109, 110, 111, 112, 113, 114, 115, 116, 117, 118, 119, 120, 121, 122, 123, 124, 125, 126, 127, 128, 129, 130, 131, 132, 133, 134, 135, 136, 137, and 138.' Caveat printed by the club: 'there is some amount of netting in front of the seating sections listed below; the height and coverage of the netting varies by section', plus 'ticket holders assume all risk of injury' and 'No seat in Tropicana Field is free from the risk of injury inherent in attending a live baseball game.' Fans are directed to 'contact the Tampa Bay Rays Ticket Office at 1-888-FAN-RAYS' for section-specific netting detail. NOTE: netting covers the ENTIRE lower bowl from pole to pole, i.e. all of 101-138 on BOTH parities; only outfield sections 139-150 are unnetted.
uncertain: TIER NAME CONFLICT, 200 LEVEL. RateYourSeats calls sections 203-224 the 'Press Level' (https://www.rateyourseats.com/tropicana-field/seating/sections/203, https://www.rateyourseats.com/tropicana-field/seating/sections/204, https://www.rateyourseats.com/tropicana-field/seating/sections/224). The club's own guide instead lists its levels as '100 Level (Field Level)', '200 Level', '300 Level', 'Club Level', 'MaintenX SkyDeck (above left field)' and 'Webull Suite Level (200 Level Premium Suites)' (https://www.mlb.com/rays/ballpark/information/guide) - it never uses 'Press Level' as a ticketed tier name. Both recorded; not reconciled. A View From My Seat separately lists both a 'Press Box' and a 'press level' area (https://aviewfrommyseat.com/venue/Tropicana+Field/).

ZONE NAME CONFLICT, 300 LEVEL. Two separate reads of the RateYourSeats section index labelled the 300-series group differently - once as 'Club Level' and once as 'Upper Deck' - and one read headed the group '300-323' while listing 324 in its contents. No 300-level section page checked (300, 301, 312, 324) printed an explicit zone name at all. `sections` records 300-324 inclusive, which both reads' contents support, but the UPPER BOUND (whether 324 is genuinely the last section) is the weakest single item in the section list and should be re-checked before generation.

300 LEVEL OPEN OR CLOSED IN 2026 - UNRESOLVED AND CONSEQUENTIAL. The upper deck has been tarped and unsold since 2019 (Wikipedia 'with upper decks tarped over'; MLB.com Apr 9 2026 '25,025 (since 2019, with upper deck closed)'), yet RateYourSeats still serves live per-section pages for 300-324 and the club's own 2026 guide still lists a '300 Level' among its levels. Against that, the club's 2026 elevator list names no 300-level stop (https://www.mlb.com/rays/ballpark/information/accessibility-guide). NO 2026-DATED OFFICIAL STATEMENT was found either way, and the Feb 27 2026 and Nov 12 2025 upgrade announcements are both silent on it. There is precedent for selective re-opening (https://www.mlb.com/news/rays-to-open-portions-of-upper-deck-for-yankees-series). Recommend generating 300-level sections but flagging them as regular-season-unavailable.

300 LEVEL PARITY NOT DIRECTLY STATED. Parity is proven by explicit quotes on the 100 level and the 200 level, and by the club's park-wide sentence 'Even-numbered sections are on the first base/right field side...Odd-numbered sections are on the third base/left field side' (https://www.mlb.com/rays/ballpark/information/guide). But NO 300-level page checked printed an odd/even sentence, and RateYourSeats gave no location text for sections 300, 312 or 324. The 300-level parity assumption rests on the club's park-wide rule plus section 301's 'desirable view from behind home plate'. High confidence, but not directly quoted.

BALDWIN GROUP CLUB LOCATION CONFLICT. RateYourSeats' zone page puts it at field level, 'Sections 106-126 along the first base line' (https://www.rateyourseats.com/tropicana-field/seating/rays-club, 'Last verified and reviewed: March 2026'), and its per-section pages give rows PP-UU. The club's own Feb 27 2026 article places The Baldwin Group Club 'on the fourth floor' (https://www.mlb.com/rays/news/rays-continue-tropicana-field-improvements-ahead-of-opening-day). These may describe a field-level seating product plus a separate fourth-floor lounge of the same name, but no source states that. Both recorded verbatim; not reconciled.

PREMIUM SECTION IDENTIFIER FORM. The addressable RateYourSeats identifiers are the URL slugs HPC103, HPC104, HPC107, HPC108 and 106C...126C, but the page HEADINGS render them as 'Home Plate Club 103' and 'Rays Club 106', and two reads of the section index rendered the index labels inconsistently (once as 'HPC103'/'106C', once as 'Home Plate Club 103'/'Rays Club 106'). `sections` records the SLUG form. Confirmed directly by fetching https://www.rateyourseats.com/tropicana-field/seating/sections/HPC103 and https://www.rateyourseats.com/tropicana-field/seating/sections/106C, both of which resolve to real pages. Also note the Home Plate Club set SKIPS 105 and 106.

ORIENTATION IS SINGLE-SOURCED AND WEAK. Only Andrew Clem's vital-statistics table gives a bearing, 'NE' (http://www.andrewclem.com/Baseball/TropicanaField.html). No club page, Wikipedia entry or Ballparks of Baseball page states a compass orientation. Because the park is a fixed dome there is no sun/shade evidence to cross-check against, which is how orientation was corroborated at open-air parks in this project. Low-to-medium confidence. Practically this matters little here: with no sun exposure, orientation drives no seat guidance at this venue.

NO OFFICIAL 2026 CAPACITY FIGURE. Every capacity number in this file traces to 25,025 (a 2019 reconfiguration figure) or to ArenaCapacity's rounded 'up to 25,000'. The Rays' own 2026 ballpark guide states no capacity. Post-hurricane reconstruction could in principle have changed the seat count and no source addresses that. Treat 25,025 as best available, not as confirmed-for-2026.

NO 2026-DATED SECTION INVENTORY. No source republished a section list after the hurricane rebuild. The `sections` array is the RateYourSeats index as served in 2026 (with Feb/March 2026 verification stamps on individual pages), but if the rebuild added, merged or retired any section, no consulted source says so. The 2026 upgrade announcements mention videoboards, sound, suites and premium clubs - not seating-bowl geometry.

SOURCE-ACCESS CAVEAT AFFECTING EVERY RATEYOURSEATS QUOTE. Direct HTTP access to rateyourseats.com is BLOCKED by this environment's egress policy (proxy returns 403 to CONNECT for www.rateyourseats.com:443), so raw HTML could not be retrieved and every RateYourSeats quote in this file was obtained through a summarising fetch tool. That tool demonstrably varied between runs on list-heavy content (the section-index labelling inconsistencies noted above). SHORT VERBATIM SENTENCES were stable and repeated identically across many independent page fetches, so the load-bearing findings - the parity rule, the seat-1 sentence, the two seat-1 Q&As, the bullpen sentence, row labels - are trustworthy. THE LONG SECTION LIST IS THE ITEM MOST EXPOSED to this limitation. Note that the four decisive facts (parity, dugouts, netting, elevators) are ALSO independently sourced from mlb.com, which was fetched without difficulty.

NO CONFLICT FOUND ON THE ITEMS THAT BROKE OTHER PARKS - recorded deliberately. Dugout side: three sources agree (club, Ballparks of Baseball, RateYourSeats). Numbering: club and RateYourSeats agree, corroborated by netting, bullpens and elevators. Seat 1: boilerplate agrees with per-section Q&A on BOTH halves. Unlike Progressive Field, no popular guide was found inverting either the dugouts or the numbering at Tropicana Field.
